fact: The ministry's report with ADEA says 103 pilot schools across the regions, 23 of them newly added and given a tablet, solar charger and connectivity, captured daily teacher and learner attendance in School-Link in a pilot that ran from May to the end of July 2018; it gives no split of the 103 by level, and its annex lists primary, combined and secondary schools.

The ministry's report with ADEA says 807 public schools out of 1,848 schools in Namibia are connected to School-Link; the figure counts schools connected, not schools entering data, covers all levels and not primary alone, and is undated, so the report's publication month is used.

The ministry's report with ADEA says the 103 pilot schools captured each day's teacher and learner attendance, with the reason for absence, and updated School-Link weekly through the second trimester ending August 2018, recording 71,387 cases of learner absence; it describes School-Link as a live system in which users enter data daily, with a learner unit record module (LURITS).

The ministry's report with ADEA lists the 103 schools piloting attendance capture in School-Link from May 2018 by name, and they include primary, combined and secondary schools; it says School-Link was approved in 2013 as the national system for all schools.

The ministry's report with ADEA says School-Link, an EDUPAC product, was introduced to the Ministry of Education, Arts and Culture in 2013, approved as the national system for all schools and offered to them free, with a helpdesk in the ministry's ICT division; the 2017-18 attendance pilot cost NAD 291,000, met jointly by ADEA and the ministry. The report gives no date for the standing arrangement, so its publication month is used.

The ministry's report with ADEA says most schools record attendance in paper registers, marked daily by teachers and summarised weekly and by trimester for the regional director, and that only most private schools and a few urban public schools use biometric clocking or a school management system; it gives no date, so the report's publication month is used.
